- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.5) — model is overly conservative, missing upward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating sustained trends.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true trend direction — especially when sentiment is trending upward.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should adjust upward by 2–3% more than the average 30d trend.
- When sentiment is negative or mixed, model should reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment shows clear momentum reversal (e.g., 2 consecutive negative sentiment values).
